verdict.rationale: Bento's docs show it ingests traces over OpenTelemetry. A developer can point a standard OTel exporter at one Bento endpoint with an auth header, use the Python OTel transport, or send from TypeScript with no Bento package, so sending traces into Bento over OTLP is directly documented. The docs do not show Bento sending or exporting traces back out over OTLP, so the 'receive' half of the story is unevidenced. missing for 10: documented OTLP export/egress of traces out of Bento, explicit OTLP protocol/endpoint specs (gRPC vs HTTP), independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can send and receive traces over OpenTelemetry (OTLP) instead of a proprietary format

citations.quote: point its exporter at one endpoint with one auth header and the traces land in Bento. In TypeScript you can do this with no Bento package at all.
JavaScript's OpenTelemetry exporters can emit JSON, so you can send traces to Bento without installing any Bento package.
Wire it into an OpenTelemetry pipeline directly when you already have one configured, and skip the analytics layer entirely.
Every span from every framework, captured over OpenTelemetry.
No rewrites. Drop in the OpenTelemetry SDK and you're instrumented.
